1) Tests for this story exist and run without reported failures via `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` (which executes `jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose`).
2) Core plugin structure and rule registry (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) are implemented in TypeScript: - src/index.ts defines RULE_NAMES, dynamically requires each rule module into a central `rules` object, and exports `rules`, `configs`, and `maintenance` along with a default export: - JSDoc: - `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` - `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Provide foundational plugin export and registration` - `@req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Gracefully handles plugin loading errors and missing dependencies` - Dynamic loading: - `const RULE_NAMES = ["require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference", "prefer-implements-annotation"] as const;` - `RULE_NAMES.forEach((name) => { try { const mod = require("./rules/" + name); rules[name] = mod.default ?? mod; } catch (error) { console.error(...); rules[name] = placeholderRule; } });` - Placeholder rule reports errors via `context.report` when a rule fails to load.
3) Plugin exports and configs are verified by unit tests (plugin registers and loads without errors; REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM): - tests/plugin-setup.test.ts: - `describe("Traceability ESLint Plugin (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)", () => { ... });` - Asserts `rules` and `configs` are defined and that `plugin.rules === rules` and `plugin.configs === configs`. - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts: - Annotated with `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` and `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE`. - Confirms the rules object’s keys exactly equal the expected list of rule names. - Confirms `configs.recommended[0].rules` contains the expected `traceability/...` keys with correct severities (errors for core rules, warn for formatting/migration) and that `configs.strict[0].rules` equals `configs.recommended[0].rules`.
4) Error handling behavior is implemented and tested (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, acceptance criterion marked [x] in story): - Implementation in src/index.ts: - Inside the dynamic loader, `console.error("[eslint-plugin-traceability] Failed to load rule \"" + name + "\": " + error.message)` is called on failure and a fallback RuleModule is installed. - Fallback RuleModule has `meta.docs.description` explaining the failure and a `create` function that always reports an ESLint problem for the Program node. - tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts: - Annotated with `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` and `@req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING`. - Mocks `../src/rules/require-branch-annotation` to throw `new Error("Test load error")`. - Requires `../src/index` and asserts `console.error` is called with a string containing `Failed to load rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error`. - Asserts the placeholder rule exists, meta.docs.description contains the failure description, and `create` → `Program` visitor calls `context.report` with a message containing `Error loading rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error`. - tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts: - Annotated with this story and `REQ-ERROR-HANDLING` and runs ESLint CLI via spawnSync, expecting non-zero status and a specific missing-annotation message, further exercising CLI-side behavior when rules execute.
5) ESLint v9 flat config integration and CLI behavior (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, Core Functionality, Integration): - eslint.config.js in this repo is a flat-config array (CommonJS export) that: - Imports `@eslint/js` and `@typescript-eslint/parser`. - Tries to load the plugin from `./src/index.js` then `./lib/src/index.js`, with CI-only failure if neither exists and a warning fallback in local dev, showing robust plugin loading behavior in tooling. - Attaches `traceability: plugin` to `plugins` when `plugin.rules` exists, across TS and JS file entries. - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts: - Annotated with `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` and `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Validate plugin registers via CLI`. - Locates the ESLint v9 CLI from the installed eslint package, uses `eslint.config.js` via `--config`, and runs with `--no-config-lookup`. - Runs multiple cases (missing/present @story, missing @req, path traversal/absolute path validations) and asserts `result.status` matches expected values, proving that the plugin loads and its rules run correctly under ESLint v9 flat config.
6) TypeScript-based implementation and testing infrastructure (REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-TEST-SETUP, Quality Standards): - tsconfig.json: - `"module": "CommonJS"`, `"target": "ES2020"`, `"declaration": true`, `"outDir": "lib"`, `"strict": true`, and includes both `src` and `tests`, matching ESLint plugin/Node best practices. - package.json devDependencies include TypeScript, Jest, @types/jest, @types/eslint, @typescript-eslint/utils, and ESLint v9, providing the required tooling. - Jest tests cover plugin setup, plugin error handling, CLI integration, config validation, and individual rules, satisfying the requirement for rule validation test infrastructure.
7) NPM package structure and publishability (REQ-NPM-PACKAGE, Quality Standards): - package.json: - `"name": "eslint-plugin-traceability"`, `"version": "1.0.5"`, `"main": "lib/src/index.js"`, `"types": "lib/src/index.d.ts"`, `"files": ["lib", "README.md", "LICENSE"]`. - `"peerDependencies": { "eslint": "^9.0.0" }` and `"engines": { "node": ">=18.18.0" }`. - Scripts for `build`, `type-check`, `lint`, and `test` ensure the plugin can be built, checked, and tested before publish. - This layout matches standard Node/ESLint plugin publishing conventions.
8) User experience and documentation (User Experience, Documentation acceptance criteria): - README.md: - Installation instructions with npm and Yarn. - Clear ESLint v9 flat-config example: - `import js from "@eslint/js";` - `import traceability from "eslint-plugin-traceability";` - `export default [js.configs.recommended, traceability.configs.recommended];` - Lists all available rules with links to rule-specific docs in docs/rules/. - Quick Start section showing how to annotate functions with @story/@req and run ESLint. - Sections on running tests and on CLI integration. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: - Step-by-step ESLint v9 flat-config setup with an explicit section on enabling this plugin (`traceability.configs.recommended`). - Covers common patterns, TypeScript integration, and troubleshooting, giving users clear guidance. - docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md: - Internal-facing development documentation of plugin structure, meta, rules, configs, TypeScript config, and build/distribution patterns, supporting the "plugin structure and development setup" documentation requirement.
Collectively, the code, configuration, and tests demonstrate that the ESLint plugin structure is correctly implemented in TypeScript, packaged and loadable as an npm ESLint plugin, integrated with ESLint v9 flat config, provides a rule registry and configuration presets, handles rule loading errors gracefully, and includes both user-facing setup documentation and internal development guidance.
